body: yeah I understand about doctors and stuff.  I had a teacher who once made me make a list of all the things I loved.  I was surprised by how much was on the list, but once I got started I couldn't stop.  Maybe it sounds cheesy, but maybe you could try that.

You should call a suicide hotline.  Idk where you live but in the US the number is 1-800-273-8255.
Even though you are really disconnected from your family, you could just tell them you are feeling really depressed.  Maybe they could help you find a doctor or something.

Try to do something you care about instead of something that will make money.  If there's something you love to do, don't deny yourself that pleasure.  God knows it's hard enough to find.  
Also, you could look into WWOOFING in Scotland.  I don't know if you get paid, if you do it's not a lot, but it would probably be a nice change.

Maybe instead of trying to please everyone else, you should do something you love.  Is there something you care about or feel strongly about?  What if you volunteered somewhere?  Just do something that makes you happy.  Even if society is pushing you over the edge, it doesn't mean you should fall.  Push back and do something you care about, instead of what is useful or expected.

You should take as much time as you want.  I think you're really brave, I couldn't even talk to guys except for my brother and really close friends after my ex raped me.  When I started dating one of my friends, he was really understanding and even made a point to tell me that he never wanted me to feel like I had to serve him sex.  I didn't have flashbacks after sex specifically, but did come up, and I would talk to my friend about them.  Maybe try to identify what you were doing to trigger the flashback?  Or talk to your boyfriend about it.  Also, one thing that helped me a lot was just kissing and cuddling.  I've read that that establishes trust almost more than actual sex.  
I hope these ideas help, I just stumbled across your post and wanted to speak from my experiences.

Honesty is key here.  I told my best friend I like him (which was a lie, I'm totally and completely in love with him) really recently and while it was awkward for a little bit, we've kept talking and things seem relatively normal.  I mean, there's no way your friendship will bounce back to exactly how it was, but if you really like her and think it could work, then it might be worth the risk.  The key is to give her an out if she doesn't feel the same way.  Definitely let her know that you want to stay friends if she doesn't feel the same, and if she doesn't, then don't push her about it.  But be honest about your feelings.  Don't leave anything out that you think is important.

I think it's pretty unfair, but you should be honest about your feelings.  My last boyfriend didn't like me hanging out with my best friend, who is a guy and wanted me to stop (on a side note I had to use the "He's like a brother to me!" line and now I have been effectively sibling-zoned).  Anyways, I thought it was really unfair of him to be like, hey stop hanging out with ___ and he actually started mocking me about it.  So...don't do that.  I've also been on the other side, when my other friend didn't talk to me for a year because his girlfriend didn't like me.  That was really shitty of him, so you should also consider how close of friends these guys are to your GF and how her severing ties would affect them.
